_note: The direction dependencies are allowed to run in src/. A package may import from its own layer or any layer below it, never above. Cycles between packages are the thing this prevents: scripts/check_static_invariants.py already refuses module-level cycles, but a package-level cycle hides behind submodule and deferred imports and shows up instead as two things that cannot be changed or tested apart. Edit this file to change the architecture, not to make a violation go away.

layers.name: foundation
layers.why: Settings, logging, the mathematical core, the quality registry and the in-process event bus. Import nothing from src above themselves; everything is free to import them. eventbus is here for a structural reason rather than a thematic one: its producers live in io, analytics, decision and orchestration and its consumer is api, so any higher placement is imported upward by everything below it. Only a package beneath all of them can be published to by all of them. agent_control -- the Claude session task, Git-safety and completion layer -- imports nothing from src, and the API (edge) reads its ledgers.

layers.name: crypto
layers.why: Curve arithmetic and key handling, on mathcore alone.

layers.name: io
layers.why: Market data in, observability out. The only layer that talks to the outside world other than api.

layers.name: analytics
layers.why: Everything that turns data into a number: features, regimes, models, fusion, tuning.

layers.name: decision
layers.why: What to do about those numbers, and what not to do. Risk sits beside execution deliberately -- a sizing rule that cannot see the order book is not a risk rule.

layers.name: orchestration
layers.why: Assembles the layers below into a running system. runtime is the platform that registers, supervises and changes those components, so it sits with the code that assembles them. terminal is the host service that supervises interactive sessions and the processes and jobs started from them; it imports only foundation (logging_setup) and nothing domain-specific, and the API (edge) reads it to register its own jobs.

layers.name: edge
layers.why: HTTP and websocket surface. Nothing below may import it -- an import of api from a domain package means the domain knows about transport.
